author: A. M. Tang
title: Maryland ZIP code 21202 had 3,050 Social Security beneficiaries in December 2024
text:
Maryland ZIP code 21202 had 3,050 Social Security beneficiaries in December 2024
A. M. Tang
ZIP code 21202 in Maryland recorded 3,050 Social Security beneficiaries in December 2024, an increase of 135 from the previous December. That is a reported 4.6% rise. All ZIP-level figures are controlled-rounded by the Social Security Administration (SSA) and should be considered approximate.
The Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance program, commonly known as Social Security, provides monthly benefits to qualified retired and disabled workers, their dependents and survivors of insured workers. Eligibility and benefit amounts are based on a worker's Social Security-covered earnings and contributions rather than financial need. OASDI is separate from Supplemental Security Income, or SSI, which provides benefits based largely on limited income and resources and is funded through general federal tax revenues rather than employment taxes.
In December 2024, retired workers were the largest reported group with 1,970 beneficiaries (64.6%), followed by disabled workers at 690 (22.6%). Widow(er)s and parents accounted for 160 (5.2%), children 215 (7%), and spouses 15 (0.5%). Retired workers ranked first and disabled workers second. Across all five categories, 2,070 beneficiaries were reported as aged 65 or older, representing about 67.9% of the total—this age group spans every category.
Compared with December 2023, reported counts rose for retired workers (+125, +6.8%), disabled workers (+10, +1.5%), and widow(er)s and parents (+5, +3.2%). Children decreased by 5 reported beneficiaries (-2.3%), while the spouse category showed no reported change. These reported figures add up to the overall ZIP code total in this case, but that alignment is not guaranteed for every ZIP code because each category is rounded independently.
For December 2024, the total reported monthly benefits for ZIP code 21202 were $4.74 million. The approximate average monthly benefit per reported beneficiary was $1,554. Both figures reflect benefits for one month only and are rounded.
The published series for ZIP code 21202 runs from 2018 through 2024, comprising seven published December readings. Over that span, the reported beneficiary count rose from 2,560 in 2018 to 3,050 in 2024, with increases recorded in each interval. These numbers reflect only the published December counts for this ZIP code; years without reported data are not included.
Maryland reported a statewide total of 1,092,693 Social Security beneficiaries in December 2024, an increase of 24,691 from a year earlier. ZIP code 21202’s reported share of the statewide total was approximately 0.3%, reflecting the rounding of ZIP-level data. The ZIP code ranked 134th out of 532 published ZIP codes in Maryland. The statewide rate was 176.1 beneficiaries per 1,000 residents in 2024, based on U.S. Census Bureau data. This is below the pooled comparison rate of 200.2 per 1,000 residents across the 50 states and the District of Columbia. These counts use ZIP Code information from SSA address records, which may not always match the beneficiary’s place of residence exactly.
| Beneficiary category | 2024 beneficiaries | 2023 beneficiaries | Change | 2024 share |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Retired workers | 1,970 | 1,845 | +125 | 64.6% |
| Disabled workers | 690 | 680 | +10 | 22.6% |
| Widow(er)s and parents | 160 | 155 | +5 | 5.2% |
| Spouses | 15 | 15 | 0 | 0.5% |
| Children | 215 | 220 | -5 | 7.0% |
| Year | Reported beneficiaries | Annual change |
|---|---|---|
| 2018 | 2,560 | n/a |
| 2019 | 2,715 | +155 |
| 2020 | 2,775 | +60 |
| 2021 | 2,790 | +15 |
| 2022 | 2,850 | +60 |
| 2023 | 2,915 | +65 |
| 2024 | 3,050 | +135 |
Beneficiary and benefit figures are drawn from OASDI Beneficiaries by State and ZIP Code, 2024, and state population data are from the U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey. Counts reflect beneficiaries in current-payment status as of December and assign ZIP Codes using SSA address records, which can reflect a representative payee’s address rather than the actual residence. ZIP-level figures are controlled-rounded, generally to the nearest five, and each category is rounded independently; category totals may not always sum to the reported ZIP total. ZIP rows below the publication threshold are omitted, so absence means unavailable, not zero, and trends reflect only published years. Statewide figures use the published state-total record. The 51-jurisdiction rate compares the statewide count to a pooled beneficiary-to-population ratio across the 50 states and District of Columbia, but is not a national rate or an average of individual state rates.
